I farm the way I know best: I keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation because that is the steadiest way for me to hold grain yield on irrigated land in Quzhou. I do not want to spread myself too thin at 65, so I will keep cotton and garlic on smaller areas where I can still manage them carefully. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it clearly helps yield and stand, and I will stay with ordinary field operations that I know well: rotary tillage for most land, enough fertilizer to push yield but not waste money, well irrigation at the key growth stages, and a limited number of pesticide sprays only when I expect the usual local problems. For this year, I will put 12 mu into the wheat-maize rotation, 2 mu into cotton, and 2.1 mu into garlic, because that gives me a balance between grain for stability and cash crops for income.
